summary: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Vasudeva is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who taught S. N. Krishna. At the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, he served as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Deputy Director (attested 2026).

Linguist and Indologist T. V. Venkatachala Sastry studied at the University of Mysore under teachers including D. L. Narasimhachar and Harogadde Manappa Nayak. He lectured at Kanakapura, St. Joseph's, and Osmania, before becoming Professor at Mysore (1984–1994).

T. Venkatacharya was an Indology scholar who held positions at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and the University of Toronto, where he was attested as Professor in 1971. His students included Yuichi Kajiyama and Shoryu Katsura.

T. W. Rhys Davids (1843–1922) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He founded the Pali Text Society and held professorships at University College London and Manchester.

Tadao Yoshikawa studied at Kyoto University, later serving as an assistant professor (1974, 1984–2000) and Ryukoku University professor (2002). Working in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he also headed the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (around 2000).

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. His career included posts at Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum (director 1988–2006), Bukkyo University, and Kyoto University of the Arts.

Tadashi Sekino (1868–1935) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1892 to 1895 and later served there as professor emeritus from around 1929 to 1935.

Tadashi Tani studied at Waseda University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as professor at the National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (c. 1989–2007) and lectured at several universities.
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He pursued his education under the instruction of teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who received his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978. He served at SOAS University of London as Professor and Reader, teaching students such as Rita Langer and Ulrich Pagel.
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998).

Taichiro Kobayashi (1901–1963) studied at Kyoto University under Sentaro Sawamura, Kitaro Nishida, and others. Specializing in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he worked at the Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts and became a professor at Kobe University in 1950.
Taido Kitamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. His career includes serving as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and holding a post (attested 1994–1999) at Shuchiin University.

Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar educated at Columbia and the Graduate Theological Union. He received Dharma transmission from Reb Anderson and taught at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Loyola University Chicago, and other institutions.

Taijo Iwata is a scholar of Buddhist studies. His career includes appointments as lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and adviser at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Taijun Inokuchi worked in Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts as lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987) at Ryukoku University, and as representative of the Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) studied at Komazawa and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, he was appointed Professor of Indian Philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1912.

Taiken Kyuma is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna by 1999 and served as an Associate Professor at Mie University between 2002 and 2008.
Taiken Tanaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was educated at Hiroshima University. He held a position as assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University, attested in 1991.
